doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Arriving in New York and getting hired by Marian McPartland
summary: With his wife's job easing money pressure, Moore got started via John Bunch's recommendation to Marian McPartland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you look at the Local 802 union book, you see an awful lot of players. And what was it like, trying to find a niche?

My wife at the time had a job in New York so it took the financial pressure off, which I think that’s the main thing. New York — in that time there was a lot more work in the town, in ‘68, but it was very frightening to me, so again I was still very insecure and I was not the kind of guy to go out and sit in in clubs and say here I am, which I’ve known in subsequent years, guys that had that kind of moxie, and I admire that, but I had a few contacts from Woody’s band and I think I played with John Bunch someplace, the piano player, and he recommended me to Marian McPartland. And I played with Marian McPartland and she liked me and hired me and that kind of got me started and gave me some credentials and she was very supportive. She played my songs, and was very encouraging. And that was kind of what got me started — working with Marian in New York.
